course_title: Clinical Skills in Psychotherapy 4: Working with complexity
course_description:
This course focuses on the clinical skills needed to engage with patients. In this fourth psychotherapy skills course you will develop your skills in assessment of mental health issues in people with complex presentations and will develop skills in formulation and treatment planning for psychotherapy interventions with complex presentations. Psychotherapy Field of Study requirements will be met by this course.

Semester 2 offering is in-person (or on-campus) and is the normal study mode for this course. Semester 1 offering is for international students only and has restricted access, with Head of School permission required for enrolment. Students requesting external enrolment in Semester 1 must contact med.enquiries@uq.edu.au

This course addresses the challenges of managing clinical complexity. We will explore why complex clinical presentations often defy conventional approaches and prove difficult to manage. Together, we will develop creative and innovative methods to deliver mental health services to individuals who struggle to access traditional mental health and psychotherapy options.

course_aims: This course focuses on dealing with clinical complexity. We will examine aspects of why complex clinical presentations are so difficult to manage and hard to apply the tried and trusted clinical approaches. We will work towards creative, innovative ways to provide appropriate mental health services to people who find it difficult to access traditional mental health and psychotherapy services.

learning_outcomes.description: Critically engage with contemporary approaches to people with complex and hard to treat mental health disorders.
Critically engage with contemporary approaches to vulnerable people with structural barriers to appropriate mental health care.
Demonstrate capacity to assess and, where appropriate, initiate and sustain psychotherapy for people with complex and treatment resistant presentations.

assessment_details.title: Complex clinical challenges - written report
assessment_details.task_description: This assignment is your opportunity to deepen into the understanding of a complex clinical problem and the barriers to treatment associated to such problem, and learn or design psychotherapeutic strategies, interventions or techniques to overcome such barriers. You will independently conduct this research effort. You should chose the complex clinical problem to be reported based on a specific case that is challenging you, or a special interest in a type of complex presentation. This report will be the written outcome of this research effort. Identify a complex clinical problem in mental health and psychotherapy field that is being challenging to you, to your service or to the psychotherapy discipline in general. This complex clinical challenge should refer to a) a challenging case you are treating that is complex due to a conjunction of biopsychosocial factors, or other features, or b) a specific clinical cohort involving a complex and specific combination of social, cultural, diagnostic or other specific features. Even though AI use is permitted, the focus of this activity is to assess your capacity to analyse and formulate knowledge, reflect, and demonstrate creative and independent thinking. If you use AI, you need to reference its use. Following UQ guidelines, this assessment will marked against a rubric that will be available for students. You should: Describe in detail the complex clinical problem you are focusing on, including a case presentation if pertinent. Identify its central characteristics, relevant background, and summarise what is known about this problem either through a) a case formulation, and/or b) a summary of clinical literature and research on the problem. Identify and describe the barriers to psychotherapeutic treatment that are associated to this complex problem, and explain how these barriers operate. Describe strategies, intervention or technique you used or propose to use to overcome these barriers to treatment for this case or clinical group. Propose a method or rationale to assess the effectiveness of the strategies you have implemented or propose to implement. Your report is written following scientific standards, with a length of 3000 word (-/+ 10%). If you plan to use AI for this report, please discuss its purpose with the course coordinator to make sure it aligns with learning objective, and then reference its use in your report. assessment_details.title: Complex clinical challenges - oral presentation
assessment_details.task_description: You will present the main findings of the report you made on a complex clinical challenge through an oral presentation to your peers. This will be followed by a Q&A led by the course coordinator in which you will respond to questions about your presentation and report, with focus on resolving barriers to treatment. This will be followed by a discussion with your peers. The duration of your presentation, of the following Q&A and open discussion will be determined by the course leader depending on the number of students and available time, but as reference should range between 20-30 minutes. Identify a complex clinical problem in mental health and psychotherapy that is challenging to you, to your service or to the psychotherapy discipline in general. This complex clinical challenge could refer to a) a specific case you are currently treating that presents with a complex conjunction of biopsychosocial factors, diagnoses, or clinical features, or b) a specific clinical cohort sharing a complex and specific combination of social, cultural, diagnostic or other specific features. You must rely on the content of your written report, and any other sources such as papers or audiovisual material previously discussed and agreed with the course coordinator. Following UQ guidelines, this assessment will marked against a rubric available to students, and it will be recorded for eventual review purposes. During your presentation you should: Briefly describe the complex clinical problem, its central characteristics, and relevant background. This could be a formulation if you are reporting a case. Identify the barriers to treatment and how they operate. Present the strategies you followed or propose to implement and explain how they worked or intend to work. Respond to question in the Q&A section and open discussion about your project. Your presentation is clear, well organised and visually appealing. Use of PowerPoint slides is recommended.
